atomic_propositions: The 2024 revision applies a risk- and evidence-based approach to laboratory biosecurity.
The guidance applies that approach to high-consequence research and other activities involving biosecurity-relevant material, technology, and/or information.

The guidance states that it provides tools and best practices at laboratory, institution, and national-regulatory levels, and at a horizontal level that includes sample collection, transport, processing, storage, and, if necessary, destruction.

The guidance describes a two-tier system involving institutional biosafety committees first and national regulatory bodies second for review and oversight of high-consequence research and work with high-consequence material.
exclusions: Do not represent WHO guidance as Malaysian law or regulatory proof.
Do not infer that any specific material, information, technology, research, or activity is biosecurity-relevant or high-consequence.
Do not infer project-specific governance, oversight, access, inventory, handling, transport, storage, destruction, reporting, control, approval, compliance, or authorization requirements.
Do not represent the historical phrase “secure handling” as direct wording from these support passages; retain the source’s narrower stated scope and examples.
Do not treat institutional committee review or oversight described in international guidance as Malaysian regulator approval.
Do not activate these propositions for live retrieval or claim use.
findings: PDF page 21 directly supports application of a risk- and evidence-based approach to laboratory biosecurity and high-consequence research or other activities involving biosecurity-relevant material, technology, or information.
PDF page 23 directly supports the three vertical levels, horizontal lifecycle examples, systematic risk-control tools, and two-tier high-consequence review/oversight model.
The historical compound claim is split into four draft propositions.
The broad historical wording “governance” is narrowed to the source’s stated levels, tools, committee function, and two-tier model; “secure handling” is not retained as attributed source wording.
limitations: This WHO publication is Tier 3 international technical guidance and does not establish Malaysian law, regulatory applicability, approval, compliance, or authorization to begin work.

The passages describe the scope and general approach of the guidance; they do not identify project-specific biosecurity risks, high-consequence status, controls, governance arrangements, transport/storage requirements, or permission for an activity.
The source’s references to national regulatory bodies do not establish the identity, position, requirement, or authority of any Malaysian regulator.
Extracted text must be compared with the immutable staged PDF; PDF page numbers are distinct from printed page labels.
